method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates in one module, the worker's questions and the claims machinery in two rule modules, worked cases in two case files; three regulative rules (written notice within 48 hours, s 38 (4) (b); commencing a s 112 proceeding within 1 year, s 113 (1); the regulator's advice within 3 months, s 231 (2)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (ACT), A2011-35, Republication No 30 (R30), effective 26 November 2025, last amended by A2025-30, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/A2011-35.txt (Schedule 4 penalty amounts as in that republication)
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is (c) Australian Capital Territory, used under CC BY 4.0; see SOURCE-LICENSE.md
seat: the worker: the person who carries out work for a business or undertaking in the ACT and is hurt, made ill, put at risk, dismissed or disadvantaged there (with the prospective worker and the person whose commercial arrangement was ended, whom Part 6 covers), and the family member asking about a worker who died (whsact-worker.l4, whsact-claims.l4)
focus: the provisions a claimant meets: incident notification, stopping unsafe work, the civil claim for discriminatory or coercive conduct, compensation, review of decisions, requests for prosecution, the time for prosecutions, industrial manslaughter and penalties

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run whsact-dates.l4 ; l4 run whsact-worker.l4 ; l4 run whsact-claims.l4 ; l4 run whsact-worker-cases.l4 ; l4 run whsact-claims-cases.l4
checks.result: 206 assertions written, 206 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07); a deliberately wrong assertion in a scratch copy showed as failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: s 5 (6), s 7; Part 3 (ss 35, 36, 37, 37A, 38 (4) (b), (7), (9)); Division 5.6 (ss 83-88) with s 103; Part 6 (ss 105, 106, 108 (1), (3), 111, 112, 113, 114 (2), (3), 115); s 184; Part 12 (ss 223 and table 223, 224, 228, 229); s 231 (1)-(2), (3) (b); s 232; s 34A; s 31 and s 34A imprisonment; Schedule 4 ss 4.1, 4.1A, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5; s 267 with s 260; s 272; s 273. Out: Part 2 duties and ss 31-33 elements, ss 104, 107, 109, 110 as offences, Part 4, Divisions 5.1-5.5 and 5.7 (except s 85), Part 7, Parts 8-11 (except s 184 and review), Divisions 13.2-13.7, Schedules 1-3, machinery. Reasons in NOTES.md.
